title: Container Orchestration

sources.title: Kubernetes: Overview
sources.supportRationale: Orchestration manages desired workload state without becoming every surrounding operations platform.

sources.title: Kubernetes: Components
sources.supportRationale: Control-plane and node components reconcile workload intent and execute containers.

sources.title: Kubernetes: Scheduler
sources.supportRationale: Placement depends on resource and policy feasibility rather than desired replica count alone.

sources.title: Kubernetes: Persistent volumes
sources.supportRationale: Persistent volume binding, reclaim and access semantics constrain stateful placement and recovery.

sources.title: Kubernetes: Liveness, readiness and startup probes
sources.supportRationale: Probe purposes/actions differ and misconfiguration can cascade.

sources.title: Google SRE: Addressing cascading failures
sources.supportRationale: Retry amplification and resource exhaustion spread failures.

sources.title: AWS: Disaster recovery strategies
sources.supportRationale: Backup/restore, standby and multi-site recovery trade recovery objectives against cost and complexity.

scenarios.theme: Three services and two engineers: should you adopt a full cluster?
scenarios.assumptions: The team needs simple deployments and has no dedicated platform operator. Traffic is modest. What decision process fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Container Orchestration to small team.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Three services and two engineers: should you adopt a full cluster?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Compare a supervised host or managed runtime against concrete availability, storage and release requirements

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Simpler hosting can impose scaling/isolation limits; more powerful orchestration can overwhelm the team’s operations budget

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Popularity and future hypothetical scale are weaker evidence than a real unmet requirement.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to orchestration, components; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: Nine workers are spread 7/1/1 across zones. Can you promise six survive any zone loss?
scenarios.assumptions: Six equal-capacity workers are required during peak and the largest zone can fail. What placement/capacity change fits?

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Container Orchestration to zone loss.

scenarios.theme: A node stops heartbeating but may still write. Is replacement alone safe?
scenarios.assumptions: The workload owns an exclusive external job. Network isolation hides the old process from the controller. What will you protect?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Container Orchestration to partition overlap.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A node stops heartbeating but may still write. Is replacement alone safe?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Use an application/data ownership protocol with fencing or equivalent authority enforcement before allowing conflicting side effects

scenarios.theme: A database slowdown restarts the entire fleet. What policy is missing?
scenarios.assumptions: Health checks classify every slow database call as a dead process and restart all API workers repeatedly. What changes?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Container Orchestration to dependency restarts.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A database slowdown restarts the entire fleet. What policy is missing?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Separate process liveness from serving readiness and dependency diagnosis, bound request/retry load and restore dependency capacity

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Removing all checks hides genuine hangs

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Aggressive deep probes also load the dependency; choose bounded signals with distinct actions and validate degraded behavior.

scenarios.theme: A rescheduled worker starts with an empty local directory. Did orchestration lose the database?
scenarios.assumptions: The service wrote durable state to a node-local path and the replacement landed on another machine. What contract must change?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Container Orchestration to storage mobility.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A rescheduled worker starts with an empty local directory. Did orchestration lose the database?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Define durable storage and data recovery ownership explicitly, choose suitable volume/data replication semantics and verify replacement against real restor

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Network storage adds cost and latency; replication can propagate bad writes

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Task mobility does not imply local data mobility or a consistent backup.

scenarios.theme: A managed platform outage reveals nobody owns application backup restoration. Who should?
scenarios.assumptions: The provider runs the control plane, but the team cannot recover its application data after deletion. What operational agreement fits?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Container Orchestration to managed boundary.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: A managed platform outage reveals nobody owns application backup restoration. Who should?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Document provider versus team duties, assign application/data recovery ownership and test a complete restore with keys, configuration and dependencies

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Delegating infrastructure removes selected work, not every failure responsibility

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Buying replication alone may improve availability without preserving recoverable historical state.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to orchestration, storage, dr; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.
